title: Receipt check never compares the receipt's amount or capture id with the signed terms
body:
## Summary
The verifier's receipt check only confirms each receipt's raw envelope is in the transcript; the receipt's signed amount and the bundle's side fields (capture_id, amount_minor) are never compared with the deal's signed amount or the PayPal capture.

## Description
crates/table-verify/src/lib.rs receipts() (the fn after audit()) loops `bundle.transcript.iter().any(|e| e.raw == receipt.raw)` and nothing else. Body::Receipt (crates/table-proto/src/envelope.rs:188) carries capture_id, amount and transcript_head, and ProofReceipt (crates/table-proto/src/proof.rs:108) carries extracted copies capture_id / amount_minor / transcript_head that a reader may display. A receipt for 13.00 on a 12.00 deal, or side fields that disagree with the signed raw, reads 'N receipt(s) inside the signed transcript' and verifies. Fixed: decode the receipt body; require amount == deal.terms.amount(), the side fields equal the signed body, and the capture id equal a stored capture answer when one exists.

## Flow
- build a bundle whose transcript holds a signed RECEIPT for 13.00 on 12.00 terms -> receipt check ok=true today
- set ProofReceipt.amount_minor to 1 -> still ok
- fix: compare body amount / capture id / head with terms, side fields and the stored capture

## Expected impact
A third party checking a deal file learns whether the receipt states the money that was agreed; could break: a legitimate partial-capture receipt (none today) would read as a failure.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the receipt line proves the receipt matches the deal, not only that it was signed
Before: 0 of 3 facts compared (amount, capture id, side-field consistency) in receipts()
After: 3 of 3 compared; a seeded wrong-amount receipt fails
Method: simulation - the instrument needs a signed two-party transcript fixture ending in a RECEIPT (transcript() re-verifies the chain), larger than the round could build
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: table-verify test: a transcript fixture ending in a signed RECEIPT with amount != terms amount (and one with ProofReceipt.amount_minor != body) must fail the receipt check; a matching one stays green

title: House page accepts two confirmed captures on one house deal
body:
## Summary
house_capture (crates/table-verify/src/house.rs order()) checks each capture follows an authorization and the buyer's approval, but never that a deal was captured at most once.

## Description
crates/table-verify/src/house.rs order() sets `captured |= m.outcome == Ok` and judges each Capture only by before(Authorize) && before(ApprovalSeen). Two Capture steps with outcome Ok on one deal both pass and the line reads 'N capture(s), each after an authorization...'. The house seller captures once per deal, so a second confirmed capture on the public page is money taken twice and should fail the check. Fixed: count confirmed captures per deal and fail above one.

## Flow
- a HouseDealView with create, approval_seen, authorize, capture(Ok), capture(Ok)
- verify_house -> house_capture ok=true today
- fix: a second Ok capture names the deal

## Expected impact
Anyone reading the glass-box house ledger sees a double charge flagged; could break: nothing known (one capture per deal is the house's only path).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the house page can show a deal was charged twice
Before: 2 Ok captures on one deal -> house_capture ok
After: 2 Ok captures -> house_capture fails naming the deal
Method: simulation - needs a HouseDealView fixture (many fields) the round did not build
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: unit test in house.rs: order() over a HouseDealView with two Ok Capture steps returns Err; one Ok capture returns Ok(true)

title: Seller-side and house qty guards in Pipeline::authority have no isolating test
body:
## Summary
Two guards in table-app's Pipeline::authority survive removal with every wallet-app test green: SellerMandate's `deal.side == Side::Seller` and HouseMandate's `deal.terms.qty == 1`.

## Description
Negative controls run this round in a throwaway worktree on crates/table-app/src/pipeline.rs Pipeline::authority: M2 (drop `deal.side == Side::Seller &&` from the SellerMandate arm) and M5 (drop `&& deal.terms.qty == 1` from the HouseMandate arm) each left gauntlet, pipeline, rescue, inbox and listing_qty all green; M1 owner ticket, M3 purchase-on-policy and M6 policy-Allow were each caught, and M4 (rescue) is now caught by rescue.rs no_rule_sends_a_rescue_invoice_even_under_the_owners_presence_threshold. A later layer (ledger reserve/countersign side checks; house tests in table-runtime) may make a survivor equivalent, so each is either a missing test or a documented equivalent mutant. Fixed: one test per guard in crates/table-app/tests/pipeline.rs that fails when the guard alone is removed, or a note naming the layer that makes it redundant.

## Flow
- remove the guard in a worktree
- cargo test -p table-app --test gauntlet --test pipeline --test rescue --test inbox --test listing_qty -> all green
- add the isolating test; seed the mutation again -> red

## Expected impact
A future edit that drops either guard is caught before review; could break: nothing (tests only).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - each money-authority guard has a test that fails without it
Before: 2 of 6 seeded guard mutations survive the wallet-app suite (M2, M5)
After: 0 of 6 survive, or each survivor documented as equivalent with the catching layer named
Method: gate - mutation probe run this round (6 mutants); building the two tests did not fit the budget
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: probe log: M1 failed=[every_refusal_comes_before_any_paypal_call]; M2 failed=[]; M3 failed=[a_purchase_never_runs_on_policy_and_the_owner_path_captures_it]; M4 failed=[] (fixed 2efd019); M5 failed=[]; M6 failed=[policy_authority_is_refused_above_clause_6_before_any_paypal_call]
instrument: re-run M2 and M5 in a worktree with the new tests: each must turn a named test red (or the card records the catching layer)

title: Never-cut H3 is credited to a test that checks one of its three clauses
body:
## Summary
The acceptance matrix credits H3 (two ACCEPTs: same terms_hash, one AUTHORIZE order, invoice_id {deal}-{attempt}) only to pipeline.rs h3_two_accepts_one_order_and_h5_..., which asserts a single order create but not intent AUTHORIZE, the invoice id shape, or equal terms hashes on both wallets.

## Description
crates/table-app/tests/pipeline.rs:421-470 asserts one POST /v2/checkout/orders and one capture. Intent and invoice_id are asserted only by gauntlet.rs f2_a_purchase_... (`"intent":"AUTHORIZE"`, `"invoice_id":"{id}-1"`), which carries F2, not H3 (acceptance.rs ids_of reads the leading ID run). The never-cut gate passes H3 on a partial test. Fixed: the H3 test asserts the create body's intent and invoice_id and buyer/seller terms-hash equality.

## Flow
- cargo test --workspace -- --list | acceptance-matrix: H3 -> 1 test
- that test has no assertion on intent, invoice_id or terms hash

## Expected impact
The never-cut H3 row means what it says; could break: nothing (test only).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the never-cut matrix row is backed by a test of all its clauses
Before: 1 of 3 H3 clauses asserted by the H3-tagged test
After: 3 of 3
Method: simulation - read the test and the matrix rule; no mutation run (the create body is built in table-paypal, outside these contexts)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: after strengthening, mutate the create body's invoice_id or intent in a worktree (table-paypal CreateOrder::body) and confirm the H3-tagged test goes red
